body.x: Daesang Wellife (CEO Hoonkyo Seo) participated in the Global Media Meetup for domestic companies and startups on September 3.

The Global Media Meetup, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, focuses on introducing the products and technologies of Korean companies and startups to the global market. It aims to provide early international coverage and business opportunities for CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and CES participants.

Daesang Wellife, a healthcare company under Daesang Group that provides lifecycle and lifestyle customized nutrition solutions, has offered tailored health solutions based on clinical research and scientific approaches for the past 30 years since launching the balanced nutrition meal replacement ‘Nucare’ in 1995.

The company’s flagship brand, ‘Nucare’, has expanded beyond meal replacement into essential nutrition supplementation and disease management for the aging population, securing its leadership in the patient food market. Specialized product lines such as nutrition for diabetic patients and growth products for children have earned strong trust from medical professionals.

Through its ‘Nucare All Protein’ brand, the company also targets the growing protein market for modern consumers, while continuing steady research and development in traditional health food categories like chlorella and red ginseng. This effort builds a comprehensive product portfolio to cater to diverse lifestyles and health goals.

With strong technology and forward-looking investments, Daesang Wellife achieved sales exceeding KRW 300 billion in 2023, reinforcing its position as a leader in the domestic health functional food market.

body.cap: San Kim, LPM of Daesang Wellife, in an interview with Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, during the Global Media Meetup held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Daesang Wellife cited innovative R&D as its growth engine. ‘Nucare’ holds the top position in Korea’s patient food market and has established itself as a personalized health solution across life stages.

The company developed Korea’s first chlorella cultivation technology, pioneering the functional ingredient market for immune enhancement. It also built market trust with Korea’s only L-arginine product, recognized by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety for functionality. Recently, its eco-friendly packaged ‘Chlorella Platinum’ won the 2025 WorldStar Global Packaging Award, highlighting both excellence and sustainability.
Global expansion continues with investments aimed at strengthening our overseas presence, including in Vietnam.

Daesang Wellife is challenging for a CES 2026 Innovation Award with its AI-based healthcare platform ‘myTHS.’ While conventional healthcare systems create information silos, the company emphasized that its flexible cloud architecture breaks them down.

Daesang Wellife said, “We integrate over 20 data points to build a complete health story that doctors don’t have time to see. Our ‘AI TAILOR’ acts as your personal high-speed advocate. It analyzes your story and delivers the most important ‘next action’ in one second. This is not just a simple risk prediction, but an accurate assessment of chronic disease. The system may be opaque, but our real-time 3D modeling makes your body transparent to you. Our technology is a fortress for personal health, returning security and power to millions with advanced encryption technology.”

body.cap: Image showing the main dashboard of the myTHS app | Image by Daesang Wellife

body.x: Daesang Wellife’s solution begins with health check-up reports, one of the most daunting aspects of healthcare. Its 3D organ modeling transforms them into tools for self-discovery, enabling users to explore and visualize their anatomy and form intuitive connections with their bodies.

The company combines this with a simple color hierarchy that serves as a universal language, offering instant clarity of health status regardless of background knowledge. This ensures accessibility for all, not just a user-friendly design.
By integrating the user’s complete health story and providing clear AI-driven next steps through ‘AI TAILOR,’ the platform replaces systemic confusion with personal clarity.

Understanding one’s body has long been a privilege reserved for experts who use complex terminology. Daesang Wellife’s platform democratizes this, creating a new visual language for health through its patented ‘AI TAILOR’ combined with the industry’s first 3D organ modeling.

The company highlighted users’ before-and-after changes, noting an average 15% improvement in chronic disease indicators, which contributes to building a more resilient society. A company representative said, “By enabling individuals to win their personal health battles, myTHS reduces healthcare inequality and strengthens communities from within.”

body.cap: Image showing how myTHS measures and diagnoses heart health | Image by Daesang Wellife

body.x: The solution also demonstrates innovation in terms of Human Security. As healthcare shifts to digital platforms, vulnerable groups unable to handle complex apps face digital exclusion, missed medications, preventable health deterioration, and isolation risks.

To break these barriers, myTHS removes digital literacy requirements with a one-button platform. A single press launches a guided health journey narrated by a friendly AI voice, turning intimidating tasks into interactive conversations.

Its exclusive AI TAILOR is built to understand seniors’ cognitive and emotional needs, transforming complex data into clear visual cues and building trust. Clinical trials showed that eliminating fear and confusion doubled adherence to healthy habits.
By addressing the digital literacy gap, myTHS offers a scalable blueprint for an equitable health future that serves all humanity, not just the tech-savvy.

Beyond digital, Daesang Wellife envisions building a seamless, integrated healthcare network that links hospitals, pharmacies, check-up centers, fitness clubs, and sports facilities with online platforms. This strategy overcomes the indirectness of online services and delivers more direct and effective health management.

The company also aims to move beyond being a health food enterprise, positioning itself as a pioneer restoring health sovereignty to underserved populations in Southeast Asia affected by technological and medical inequality. By delivering critical health information clearly and straightforwardly, it aims to usher in a new era of disease prevention and improved quality of life. In countries like Vietnam, the AI healthcare platform ‘myTHS’ is expected to serve as a remedy to address the health illiteracy crisis.

CEO Hoonkyo Seo said, “Daesang Wellife will continue to contribute to improving quality of life with innovative products and services under our philosophy of being a ‘partner in healthy living.’ We will grow into a wellness company recognized not only in Korea but also in the global market.”

body.x: Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology.
